headline: Revenue accelerates, guidance raised despite Mideast drag
summary_short: Airbnb reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $2.678 billion, up 17.9% y/y and above the high end of its own guidance, with net income of $160 million (+3.9% y/y) and diluted EPS of $0.26.
summary_long: Revenue grew 17.9% y/y to $2.678 billion (15% ex-FX), beating guidance on 19% Gross Booking Value growth and 9% growth in Nights and Seats Booked. Net income of $160 million rose only slightly y/y: higher revenue and cost efficiencies were offset by marketing spend, a ~$70 million deferred-tax charge, and a ~$70 million equity-sale gain; Adjusted EBITDA was $519 million (19% margin), up 24% y/y. Free cash flow was $1.7 billion, down slightly y/y on Reserve Now, Pay Later timing. Airbnb repurchased $1.1 billion of stock and issued $2.5 billion of new notes to repay maturing converts. FY2026 revenue-growth guidance raised to low-to-mid teens, margin to at least 35%, Q2 revenue guided to $3.54-$3.60 billion.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by strong Nights and Seats Booked growth and a meaningful ADR increase, aided by an FX tailwind, with GBV up 19% y/y.

Higher revenue and operating-expense efficiencies (including customer support) were offset by continued sales and marketing investment, a ~$70M one-time gain on sale of an equity investment, and a ~$70M deferred-tax adjustment from a U.S. tax law change.
Free cash flow declined slightly y/y due to the working-capital impact of continued Reserve Now, Pay Later expansion, which shifts guest payments later and lowers unearned fees in Q1/Q2.

2026 revenue guidance was raised to low-to-mid-teens growth and Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to at least 35%, reflecting monetization improvements from a simplified fee structure and insurance programs.
